s.t: Breastfist opened their debut album Tickly Shimmers with it, and its video stars the band flapping across the screen in technicolour beaks.
s.src: Miami New Times: Breastfist Gets Playfully Raunchy and Deeply Funky at GroundUp Music Festival
s.q: The album’s opening number, “A Lickin,” is a slow-burning, percussion-driven sing-along ... The track was complemented by an aviary acid trip of a music video that stars the Breastfist bandmates as they flap across the screen while wearing technicolor beaks.

s.t: Breastfist’s drummer Bill Campbell wrote its words and music on his own, and on the record he sings and plays a Wurlitzer as well as the drums.
s.q: Bill Campbell-drums, vox, wurlitzer ... words and music by Bill Campbell © 2012 Earth Genius Music, SESAC

s.t: Tickly Shimmers lists its guests as “Special Guestfists”: on ‘A Lickin’ that was Christina Courtin, playing the strings.
s.q: Special Guestfists: Magic Face- triple mouth candies on "Booty" Christina Courtin- strings on "a Lickin"

f.t: They got their name in Prospect Park in 2007, when Bill Campbell’s girlfriend mispronounced “breakfast” and the slip stuck.
f.q: It was 2007 when Campbell, along with the group’s cofounder Alan Hampton, ... The New York City residents were mulling over their options in Prospect Park when the tongue-in-cheek band name was born through a slip of the tongue: Campbell’s girlfriend mispronounced “breakfast,” and the handle stuck.

f.t: On tour with Snarky Puppy, its leader Michael League played with them in a head-to-toe costume and light-up dinosaur-feet slippers, even dancing differently so nobody knew.
f.q: he would introduce the band in plainclothes and then run backstage to conceal his identity with a head-to-toe costume. “The audience wouldn’t know it was him!” Campbell laughs. “He even went as far as changing the way he moved and danced while playing. He was wearing these dinosaur-feet light-up slippers

f.t: Drummer Bill Campbell and bassist Alan Hampton started the band because, as sidemen, they were tired of being told not to play certain grooves and backbeats.
f.q: “We started this band as a way to do the things that other people wouldn’t let us do as sidemen.” It was 2007 when Campbell, along with the group’s cofounder Alan Hampton, got tired of being told not to play certain grooves or backbeats while performing as members of other projects.

f.t: When Michael League invited them to his GroundUp label in 2014, Bill Campbell didn’t want to re-release Tickly Shimmers there; they joined three years later with Amuse Deuce.
f.q: in 2014 the Snarky Puppy figurehead reached out to ask if Breastfist would be interested in joining the label. But Campbell didn’t want to re-release Tickly Shimmers as a GroundUp record, so instead suggested revisiting the idea when he had a new album finished. Three years later, Amuse Deuce was completed.

f.t: Supporting Snarky Puppy on a tight budget, Bill Campbell brought just one other bandmate, and Snarky Puppy’s own musicians learned Breastfist’s songs to play them.
f.q: Owing to budget restrictions, Campbell would travel only with one other band member, leaving Snarky Puppy musicians to learn Breastfist’s catalogue and perform their tunes.
